g.text: curb places on Terrebonne today (5.5 m)

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2428

g.text: Rue de Terrebonne itself: automobiles, private places and curb

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: The 143 buildings of five dwellings or fewer on the street, judged from street level on Nov. 12, 2026 (230 dwellings).

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Blue: their modelled automobiles. Green: their private places, counted lot by lot. Orange: the street's one parking band today.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Not in the figure: the 6 larger buildings (246 dwellings; 5 with an underground garage whose places cannot be counted), garage interiors, places in tandem

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: (266 places in all on the small lots), the cross streets' curb, visitors. On a night of 2015 the City's LiDAR shows 253 cars on the lots along the street and 183 at its curbs.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Sources: SAAQ, vehicles released under the access Act (file 03.06.34729), December 31, 2024, type inferred; Statistics Canada, 2021 Census;

g.text: City of Montréal, géobase, parking-sign inventory and assessment roll (CC BY 4.0). Automobiles below the FSA are MODELLED, not measured.
